input.standard: ASTM E741 (concentration decay, single zone); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the volume of air served by scrubber-1-v10, as V = Qe * tau from the CO2 rise at reduced speed and the decay at full speed.

steps.why: Rise: reduce the scrubber to the signed speed floor so CO2 climbs toward a higher equilibrium. Hatch-1-v10 held closed.
Decay: full speed (Qe 1 m3/min), record the decay for about one time constant (first guess V=30 m3, tau=30 min). Hatch held closed as in step 1.

abort.when: CO2 at or above limits.co2AbortPpm (3000 ppm)
the device refuses a step's command
battery state of charge under 40 percent
CDR out of the 45-120 bpm band, monitoring lost, or one more person in the lab (the source changes and the curve is invalid)

monitoring.reason: CDR (J. Picard) is the only occupant of the Lab, the volume whose CO2 is raised; hab-b (FE-1, FE-2, FE-3) is not under test and the hatch stays closed.

expected.rise: During step 1 (30% speed, Qe about 0.3 m3/min) CO2 should climb from about 1450 ppm toward a higher equilibrium. One awake occupant gives 0.38 L/min, so G/Qe alone is about 1270 ppm above the zero-CO2 removal level; the net rise is slow (tau about 100 min for V=30 m3), so only part of the curve is seen. If the rise is under about 100 ppm, tau at step 1 is not usable and V is taken from the decay alone.
expected.decay: During step 2 (100%, Qe 1 m3/min) CO2 should fall toward its equilibrium with tau = V/Qe, about 30 min for a first guess V=30 m3 (plus the 3.33 min scrubber lag). Fit C(t)=C_eq+(C_0-C_eq)exp(-t/tau) and compute V_lab = 1 m3/min * tau; expect V_lab within 10 to 200 m3, nominally about 30 m3.
expected.refutation: A decay that does not settle to a single-exponential fit, or a CO2 in hab-b that moves together with the lab's, shows the lab is not one isolated zone (exchange through the closed hatch-1-v10, design 3 m3/min) and V_lab is then an overestimate of the served volume. A change in occupants or a refused speed command invalidates the curve.

hypotheses: The Lab is one well-mixed zone.

Exchange through the closed hatch-1-v10 is not measured and is NOT assumed zero; the station-topology design flow with the hatch closed is 3 m3/min, which is comparable to the scrubber's flow. The hab-b CO2 (co2-2-v10) is recorded each minute to show whether the opening exchanges air.
The occupant (CDR, 1 person, awake, 0.38 L/min) stays in the Lab at constant activity during the test.
The scrubber's effective flow scales with speed: Qe = 1 m3/min at 100% and about 0.3 m3/min at 30%; effective flow at full speed is taken from the datasheet.
Records: lab CO2 every 1 minute, speed commands and whether accepted, hab-b CO2 every minute.
First guess of the volume is 30 m3 (factory default, stated as a guess only) used only to size the durations.
